title: Halley Ventures — account scout & outbound gameplan
content:
Quick scout notes and raw outreach draft for Halley Ventures (early-stage fintech/marketplace focused VC + portfolio ops).

Snapshot / why it looks promising
- HQ: SF; ~120 employees (LinkedIn), aggressive portfolio support org — they run a few vertical programs and offer technical co-builds for portfolio startups.
- Recent public activity: sponsoring accelerator cohort (Dec 2025), published a guide on "AI for customer support" (blog).
- Tech signal: several portfolio companies list 'custom ML/AI' on job posts; several founders mentioned running small internal LLM experiments.
- Why Redwood fits: they likely need cost-predictable inference and options for private deployments for portfolio companies handling PII/fintech data. Also good angle for a pilot as part of their accelerator (value = reduce token costs + improve latency for demo day apps).

Primary contacts (public / inferred)
- Eva Morales — Head, Portfolio Ops (LinkedIn — frequently posts about product/tech enablement) — likely main sponsor for any partnership.
- Deepak Srinivasan — CTO (portfolio platform) — cares about infra and vendor lock-in.
- Ria Patel — Program Manager, accelerator (day-to-day operations).
- Secondary: technical leads at a couple of portfolio startups (we could ask for intros if Eva is open).

Signal checks / tech stack notes (from public job posts + blog)
- Infrastructure: heavy AWS usage (EKS + RDS) and some GCP for analytics.
- Security/compliance: references to SOC2 readiness for portfolio onboarding.
- Current ML posture: mostly hosted small models, experiments on OpenAI and self-hosted smaller models. Evidence of interest in cheaper embeddings and on-prem options for regulated startups.

Value props to lead with (short list)
- Cost predictability: reserved capacity (Dedicated) that can be packaged as a cohort discount for accelerator participants.
- Private deployment option for regulated fintech startups in their portfolio (VPC or on-prem appliance).
- Developer DX: fast onboarding + example integrations (linear templates, sample repos) so startups can ship features before demo day.
- Observability & regressions: tie into accelerator's QA for model outputs across startups.

Initial outbound hypothesis / angle
- Not a cold sell on model access. Lead with "accelerator enablement + pilot" — offer a low-friction technical workshop + a 6-week pilot for 2-3 startups. Value: demo-day-ready LLM features with capped cost and SLOs.

Draft 1: short email (for Eva Morales)
Subject: Helping Halley portfolio ship demo-day LLM features
Hi Eva —
I saw Halley’s accelerator announcement and the guide you put out on AI for support — congrats. We help accelerator teams get portfolio startups from prototypes to production-ready LLM features (low token costs, predictable latency, private deployment where needed).
Would you be open to a 20–30 min call about a free cohort pilot (2–3 startups) — we handle integration templates, a short performance evaluation, and a clear cost forecast for each team?
Happy to share a short one-pager and a sample integration repo.
— Marcus

Sequence idea (timing + channel)
- Day 0: Intro email to Eva (above) + LinkedIn note referencing accelerator blog.
- Day 3: Short follow-up emphasizing cohort pilot + feedback from similar accelerator (one-liner case study).
- Day 8: Quick note to Ria (program manager) with a concrete workshop outline (2-hour technical onboarding).
- Day 14: If no response, one final value-add email with a short checklist: "3 quick ways your startups can save 40% on LLM costs this quarter".
- Day 21: If still no, try warm intro via mutual connections (Jonah/Aria to check).

Call prep: 20–30 min intro call (what to ask / goals)
- Quick intros + goals for accelerator this cycle (demo day KPIs).
- How many startups have LLM features planned? For which verticals?
- Current infra constraints (VPC / SOC2 / KMS needs).
- Typical latency/cost pain points they see.
- Who would run the technical onboarding for pilot on their side? (engineer contact)
- Quick note on success metrics we propose: 50–70% token cost reduction vs. hosted baseline OR 50–100ms median latency improvement OR 1 demo-ready feature per startup.

Objections and framing (script / quick responses)
- Objection: "We already use X vendor (OpenAI / Anthropic)"
  Response: "Totally — we don't force a model change. Redwood sits as a serving layer and routing fabric: for demo-day teams we can deliver predictable cost/latency and private deployments when needed, while preserving familiar models or running compatible open weights."
- Objection: "Security / compliance concerns for portfolio data"
  Response: "We can provision a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) and support KMS/HSM integration + audit logs. We also offer limited-data pilots where only synthetic/test datasets are used initially."
- Objection: "Too much work for startups"
  Response: "We provide integration templates (Node/Python SDKs), a 2-hour workshop, and an engineer-led onboarding (we do the heavy lifting)."

Pilot proposal (6-week, high level)
- Week 0: Kickoff + discovery (2 hrs) — select 2–3 pilot startups, collect minimal access.
- Week 1–2: Integration + perf baseline (we run tests, run cost sims).
- Week 3–4: Optimize (batching, KV-prefix caching, quantization guidance) + short training for startup engineers.
- Week 5: UAT / demo polish (latency checks, streaming).
- Week 6: Presentation at a workshop + deliverable: per-startup cost model and runbook.
Success metrics: per-startup cost forecast, median latency numbers, a deployable integration template.
Commercial ask: cohort Pilot waived for Halley (in exchange for intro credits / case study). Follow-on: packaged Dedicated discounts for portfolio customers (contract terms to be discussed).

Competition / risk map (notes)
- They already use hosted APIs — risk: they prefer zero infra ops. Mitigation: offer a managed Dedicated option and emphasize dev DX.
- Another risk: internal procurement constraints for non-profits startups. Mitigation: flexible pricing and pilot waiver.

Notes to self / tactical TODOs
- Jonah to surface any mutual connections to Eva (check LinkedIn + intro via Aria).
- Draft 1-pager + cohort one-pager (Arielle to help with numbers).
- Prepare a 2-hour workshop agenda + sample repo (repo PR #7 linked above).
- Prepare two small case snippets showing cost delta (hosted vs. dedicated) for a 1M token/month workload.
- Get legal to confirm pilot T&Cs for "no-cost" cohorts (JIRA:GT-1889).

Open questions / follow-ups
- What is their procurement timeline for accelerator vendors? (ask on intro call)
- Do portfolio companies require SOC2-level attestation? If yes, what's the gap?
- Which models are their startups already using (OpenAI vs. open weights)? Need to confirm for compatibility planning.

Short call script (first 5 mins)
- Hi Eva — quick thanks for the accelerator — can I ask how many portfolio companies will demo LLM features this cohort?
- Quick 30s about Redwood: predictable inference (cost & latency), private deploys for regulated apps, and a fast onboarding for developer teams.
- Ask about 1–2 pain points and propose a 6-week cohort pilot.

Fallbacks / alternate angles
- If portfolio ops uninterested, pivot to direct outreach to CTO / engineering leads at top 3 startups.
- Offer an "office hours" session during their onboarding week to capture interest without a formal pilot ask.

Next actions (this doc owner)
- [ ] Create 1-pager + pricing appendix (due 2026-03-17) — assign Arielle.
- [ ] Draft intro email variations (short + long) — me (Marcus).
- [ ] Repo: open PR with sample integration + README (link above) — Jonah to finalize.
- [ ] Ask Legal about pilot T&Cs — link to JIRA:GT-1889.

Random notes / fragments (scratch)
- Possible intro line: "We helped X accelerator reduce demo-day failures by shipping reliable LLM features for 8 startups in one cohort" (need permission to use names).
- Workshop title option: "LLM features that don't blow your budget"
- Consider a small grant (credit) model for the most promising startup in the cohort (marketing win).

-- end of raw scout / outreach draft --
